requested_by: Grace Whitfield, IT Security Manager, Larkspur Freight Co
title: Explain Monday's sign-in results and prove the Okta sign-on policies work as designed
situation: Larkspur Freight Co moved to Okta Identity Engine (OIE) last month. On Monday the help desk received complaints: an administrator abroad was locked out, a new admin was asked to set up Okta Verify, a contractor could not open the finance system, and one sales rep was refused while another was let in without a password. Security wants each of the 16 sign-in attempts explained by the exact policy and rule that decided it before anyone changes a setting.
your_task: Check every attempt against the network zones first: requests from an active blocklist zone, such as known bad IP addresses or anonymizing services like Tor, are refused before authentication.

Find the global session policy (GSP) that applies to the user's groups and the first rule that matches; note the primary factor, whether multifactor authentication (MFA) is required and the session lifetime.
Find the first matching rule of the app's authentication policy, checking groups, network zone, device registration, device management and device assurance, and note the assurance it asks for.

Combine both policies, compare them with the authenticators the user has enrolled and presented, and record the outcome, including whether the enrollment policy lets the user enroll the missing authenticator.
why_it_matters: In OIE an app sign-in must satisfy both the global session policy and the app's authentication policy, and policies are checked in priority order with the first matching rule winning. A rule in the wrong place, a deactivated blocklist zone or an enrollment policy that disables the only phishing-resistant authenticator can either lock out the people who need access or let an attacker in with a stolen password.
done_when: All 16 attempts have an outcome: ACCESS_GRANTED, MFA_REQUIRED_SATISFIED, DENIED_BY_GLOBAL_SESSION_POLICY, DENIED_BY_AUTHENTICATION_POLICY, DENIED_BLOCKED_ZONE, ENROLLMENT_REQUIRED or INSUFFICIENT_AUTHENTICATORS.
Each attempt names the blocklist zone, or the global session policy rule and the authentication policy rule, that decided it.
Every enrollment outcome lists the authenticators the user may enroll.
The deactivated blocklist zone found in the logs is reported to Security.

glossary.Okta Identity Engine (OIE): The current Okta platform, where app access is controlled by global session and authentication policies.
glossary.Network zone: A named list of IP ranges, or of countries, autonomous system numbers (ASNs) and anonymizer types, used in policy rules or as a blocklist.
glossary.Global session policy (GSP): The org-wide policy, assigned to groups, that controls how an Okta session is created and how long it lasts.
glossary.Authentication policy: The policy attached to an app that decides who may open it and with what level of assurance.
glossary.Authenticator enrollment policy: The policy that sets each authenticator as required, optional or disabled for a group.
glossary.Factor types: Knowledge (something you know), possession (something you have) and inherence (something you are).
glossary.Phishing-resistant authenticator: An authenticator, such as Okta FastPass or a FIDO2 (WebAuthn) security key, bound to the real site so a fake page cannot replay it.
glossary.Device assurance policy: A set of device requirements, such as minimum operating system version and disk encryption, that a device must meet.

talking_point: Traced 16 Okta sign-in attempts to the exact policy and rule that decided each one: 5 granted (4 after multifactor authentication), 7 denied (2 by blocklist zones before authentication, 3 by the global session policy and 2 by app authentication policies), 2 users prompted to enroll a missing authenticator and 2 who presented the wrong authenticators, and found a deactivated blocklist zone that no longer protects the retired VPN range.
